resources.string:
Turn your phone into a Contax T3.

The viewfinder shows the real optical world; each press of the shutter advances a 36-frame roll; when the roll is done you send it to the darkroom, and the film engine develops every frame with that roll's recipe.

Until it is developed, nobody knows what you got — that is the fun of film.

This project uses the GPL-3.0 SpektraLab film simulation engine and is therefore distributed under GPL-3.0-or-later as well: you may freely use, modify and redistribute it, provided you release your source under the same license and keep the notices.\nThe repository is not public yet; per the license, the source is provided on request.

resources.string:
Like real film, load a roll before you shoot. PORTRA 400 (warm portrait tones) is already loaded — you can shoot right away.

· Tap the film icon, bottom left: change roll
· Each film shapes the final look — portrait, landscape, B&W, slide all differ
· 36 frames per roll, developed only when it is full

When a roll is full the body prompts to rewind. Open the darkroom and develop — finished frames land in the gallery.\n\nAn empty gallery before developing isn\'t a bug: the negatives are still in the roll. The first roll comes with reminders.

· Tap the viewfinder: focus
· Swipe up or down inside the frame: exposure
· Press the shutter: film advances

Shutter bar cycles the flash. Settings panel (side key): white balance, RAW negative, colour strength, develop quality, film border. The look is fixed in development.
Tap Develop on this roll to see your first print
Frame 1/36 · develop the full roll in the darkroom

All 36 frames are shot. Develop the roll for prints.

Logged right after each shot — no developing needed. Each row is one external-flash frame with power / ISO / shutter / distance / brightness. Mark it good or bad here, then filter by marks when deriving TTL.
No external-flash calibration samples yet. Switch to the external flash mode (Pro mode recommended), take one shot, and come back — no developing needed.
The roll has frames, but none were shot in external flash mode (calibration is only logged in EXT). Switch the body flash dial to EXT, connect the A2, and take another shot.
Samples (sample list / good-bad marks) are logged in external flash mode only by default; switch to all photos to issue sample ids for every frame (power/distance remain flash-only).
A roll holds 36 frames; only the first 36 were taken

Auto pairs each stock with its maker\'s recommended paper (Kodak negatives on Portra Endura, cine film on Kodak 2383). Tap above to pick one yourself.

The negatives are still in the roll. Shoot a full roll, rewind, then develop in the darkroom — prints appear here.
Rolls waiting to be developed · tap to develop

Engineering Mode is an expert panel for enthusiasts: hand-tune input exposure, enlarger exposure, and the emulsion and print-layer parameters so every roll comes out the way you want.

A one-time purchase, not a subscription — buy once and keep it forever. Reinstalling or switching phones restores it at no extra charge.

Relic Cam itself has no network permission; the purchase is handled by the app store you installed the app from, so your photos still cannot leave this phone.

Sonnar softness on film (part of the body, not per roll)
0 = off (digital-sharp) · 4 invisible · 8 slight · 12 default · 20 soft · 35 dreamy. Takes effect on the next development.
Undo the extra colour added by the phone ISP (JPG / import only)

Default 70% (v73: raised after feedback that JPG still looked too saturated, interpolated from the 2026-11-08 three-step real-device calibration; the full-scale ceiling went from 35% to 45%) · 0 = off (pixel-identical to the previous version) · 100% looks pale and slightly bright. The Colour strength row in the camera settings panel shares this same value: Standard / Soft / Original, with Custom shown for any in-between value. One roll, one baseline: the first frame sets the strength and all 36 frames share it, so a roll never shifts in colour. Flat, night and near-monochrome scenes are damped or skipped. Device-agnostic: it measures how much the input was already graded by the ISP, so every phone gets its own strength. JPG and imported photos only; RAW is untouched and no film/printing parameter is changed. Takes effect on the next development.

Capture RAW (16-bit Bayer, bypassing the ISP tone mapping / AWB / multi-frame stacking) alongside JPEG. The DNG is kept as the negative (~25–40MB each) and developed through the engine RAW session. Falls back to the JPEG path on any failure.
Fix skin tone (yellowish) with enlarger filters

Yellowish skin: drag warmth toward cool/fair; add a touch of magenta if still yellow. The two filters alone are very weak (full scale moves only a level or two) — raise filter strength to see real change. Defaults +1.00/+0.10, strength 15; strength 0 = off. Print output only (lab-scan styles keep their own signature); takes effect on the next development.
